company: PM Capital Global Opportunities Fund Limited
title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Person
tiers.description: Key management personnel, such as executive and non-executive directors, officers and employees of the Company, the Investment Manager (PM Capital Pty Limited) and its related bodies corporate from time to time. Subject to all substantive prohibitions and the trading window/Blackout Period regime.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Restricted Persons who are executive or non-executive directors. Distinguished only for post-trade reporting: must report dealings to the Company Secretary within 2 business days (versus 'as soon as practicable' for other Restricted Persons), and must enter into a Guidance Note 22 notification agreement with the Company.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A person the Restricted Person (Principal) can be regarded as having investment control or influence over, including a family member, a nominee (including an investment manager managing funds on the Principal's behalf), a trust of which the Principal or a family member/family-controlled company is trustee or beneficiary, a person in partnership with the Principal, or a company the Principal controls. Subject to the same substantive rules as the Restricted Person they are connected to.

definitions.hedging_definition: derivative instruments or other products associated with Company Securities which operate to limit the direct economic risk of their holding in Company Securities

windows.start_anchor: one hour after the Company announces to the ASX its estimated Net Tangible Assets
windows.end_anchor: end of the last Trading Day before the day on which the Company announces its next estimated Net Tangible Asset value

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days before the Company's half year/full year results are scheduled for release, or before the Company announces a dividend or other capital management initiative that might have a material share price impact
windows.end_anchor: commencement of trading on the first trading day after such release or announcement

windows.start_anchor: commencement of on-market share purchases under the Company's dividend reinvestment plan (DRP), for Restricted Persons with knowledge of, or day-to-day management/trading-instruction responsibility for, those purchases
windows.end_anchor: cessation of such on-market DRP purchases

windows.start_anchor: commencement of an on-market share buy-back program, for Restricted Persons aware of or involved in operating it

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may decide any other period as a Blackout Period from time to time. Not expressly stated to be confidential.

rules.detail: 'Derivatives' is defined broadly (put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, structured products, swaps, CFDs, spread bets, caps and collars, or any other hedging or investment arrangement) with no venue limit, so an OTC put/call collar is squarely caught. Entering such a transaction to limit the direct economic risk of a holding is prohibited by default; a written consent application may be made under 6.2.5, but the Company Secretary 'will generally withhold' consent unless special circumstances (e.g. financial hardship, court order) exist and the Chair agrees, so this is not a routine clearance path for a wealth-management-motivated collar.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons (or their Associates) are prohibited from entering into transactions: in derivative instruments or other products associated with Company Securities which operate to limit the direct economic risk of their holding in Company Securities.

rules.detail: The same clause functions as the hedging prohibition (no separate 'hedging' definition exists): any product that limits the direct economic risk of a holding is banned absent written consent, which is 'generally withheld' outside special circumstances such as financial hardship or a court order.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons (or their Associates) are prohibited from entering into transactions: in derivative instruments or other products associated with Company Securities which operate to limit the direct economic risk of their holding in Company Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar structure is an 'other product associated with Company Securities which operate to limit the direct economic risk' of the holding, so it is caught by the same prohibition and narrow consent gateway as derivatives.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons (or their Associates) are prohibited from entering into transactions: in derivative instruments or other products associated with Company Securities which operate to limit the direct economic risk of their holding in Company Securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is prohibited by default; a consent application may be made under 6.2.5 but is generally refused absent special circumstances.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons (or their Associates) are prohibited from entering into transactions: ... which amount to 'short selling' of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
'Contracts for difference' are expressly listed within the definition of 'Derivatives' and so are prohibited by default, with the same narrow written-consent route as other derivatives.
rules.evidence: Derivatives ... includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Company Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.

rules.detail: Margin lending of Company Securities is prohibited unless conducted with the prior written consent of the Company Secretary (or delegate), after consultation with the Chair; that consent is assessed under the same 'generally withhold unless special circumstances' standard as derivatives and short selling. Once validly consented, a secured lender's later enforcement sale is excluded from the Policy entirely (clause 7).
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons (or their Associates) are prohibited from entering into transactions: ... which amounts to margin lending of Company Securities conducted without the prior written consent of the Company Secretary (or their delegate), after consultation with the Chair.

rules.detail: Granting a charge or lien is not separately named; a pledge of Company Securities to secure a loan would likely be treated as 'margin lending of Company Securities' and require the same prior written consent of the Company Secretary after Chair consultation.
rules.evidence: which amounts to margin lending of Company Securities conducted without the prior written consent of the Company Secretary (or their delegate), after consultation with the Chair.

rules.detail: The only named secured financing structure is margin lending of Company Securities, requiring prior written Company Secretary consent (after Chair consultation); a validly consented arrangement's forced-sale enforcement is excluded from the Policy altogether.
rules.evidence: A disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement which has been conducted with the prior written consent of the Company Secretary (or their delegate), after consultation with the Chair.

rules.detail: Selling within 3 months of buying is prohibited unless the Company Secretary (or delegate) gives prior written consent under the same exceptional-circumstances standard; selling immediately after conversion/exercise of a security is expressly carved out and not regarded as short-term trading.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons (or their Associates) must not engage in short-term trading of any Company Securities (for example selling the Company Securities within 3 months of buying them) unless prior written consent has been provided by the Company Secretary (or their delegate) in accordance with clause 6.2.5.

The Company Secretary (or their delegate) will generally withhold prior written consent unless special circumstances exist (such as financial hardship or a court order requiring the sale of securities) and the Chair has agreed to the granting of consent.

financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons/Directors: trigger is entering into a margin lending arrangement over Company Securities; requires prior written consent of the Company Secretary (or delegate) after consultation with the Chair, before conducting it; no separate periodic financing disclosure beyond the general holdings/dealings reporting to the Company Secretary (as soon as practicable; within 2 business days for Directors).

external_documents: ASX Listing Rules Guidance Note 22 (Director notification agreement)
exemption_authority: Company Secretary (or delegate), with the Chair's agreement, may grant written consent to deal outside a trading window, during a Blackout Period, or to engage in short-term trading, derivatives transactions, short selling or margin lending, but will generally withhold consent unless special circumstances exist (such as financial hardship or a court order requiring a sale) and never where the applicant may hold Inside Information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives ... includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Company Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition of 'Derivatives' expressly names 'caps and collars' among the instruments caught by the ban on transactions that limit the direct economic risk of a holding, so a bank-written funded collar is squarely and specifically targeted, not merely swept in generically.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary (or their delegate) will generally withhold prior written consent unless special circumstances exist (such as financial hardship or a court order requiring the sale of securities) and the Chair has agreed to the granting of consent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only route to clearance for a collar or margin loan uses the same high bar as hardship sales; an ordinary wealth-management-motivated collar is unlikely to be approved even though the Policy formally permits an application.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced-sale exclusion conditioned on prior consent
bespoke_clauses.clause: A disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement which has been conducted with the prior written consent of the Company Secretary (or their delegate), after consultation with the Chair.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The forced-sale carve-out only protects a margin lending arrangement that itself had prior written consent; an unconsented loan gets no such protection, so the bank should confirm consent was obtained for the financing leg before relying on an unencumbered enforcement path.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associate means someone that a Restricted Person (the Principal) can be regarded as having investment control or influence over. Such person might include: a family member ...; a nominee ... (including an investment manager managing funds on the Principal's behalf); a trust ...; a person in partnership ...; and a company that the Principal controls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Investment control/influence tests catch nominees, investment managers acting for the Principal, and controlled trusts/companies, so routing the collar or loan through a related vehicle does not escape the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each trading window opens one hour after the Company announces to the ASX its estimated Net Tangible Assets and closes at the end of the last Trading Day before the day on which the Company announces its next estimated Net Tangible Asset value.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because NTA is announced weekly and monthly, the default 'open' trading window is narrow and recurring; even if consent for a collar were obtained, execution timing would still need to fit within these short windows and outside the separate results/DRP/buy-back Blackout Periods.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar is not realistically available under this policy: the definition of 'Derivatives' expressly names 'caps and collars' among the instruments banned from limiting the direct economic risk of a Restricted Person's (or Associate's) holding in Company Securities, and while a written consent application can formally be made under clause 6.2.5, the Company Secretary 'will generally withhold' consent unless special circumstances such as financial hardship or a court order exist and the Chair agrees, a bar aimed at forced sales rather than routine hedging or financing transactions. The loan leg fares only slightly better: margin lending of Company Securities is similarly prohibited unless the Company Secretary gives prior written consent after consulting the Chair under the same narrow standard, though once validly consented a secured lender's later enforcement sale is excluded from the Policy altogether, including during a Blackout Period. Any permitted dealing must in any event occur within the narrow, recurring trading window (opening an hour after each NTA announcement and closing before the next) and outside the results/dividend, DRP and buy-back Blackout Periods, and never while Inside Information is held. As a listed investment company, the Policy has no employee equity-vesting concept, so there is no vested/unvested distinction to exploit. Overall: the collar's derivative legs are expressly and specifically prohibited in the ordinary course, and even the financing leg needs a rarely-granted consent, so a funded collar cannot practically be structured under this policy.
